item.title: FEDUSA elects new leadership
item.dc:creator: Thabiso Malesele
item.description: All seven National Office Bearer positions were uncontested.
item.content:encoded:
The Federation of Unions of South Africa (FEDUSA) has elected new leadership at its 8th National Congress in Kempton Park.

Refitlhile Baloyi from the Public Servants Association takes over the reins as the new FEDUSA President, succeeding Godfrey Selematsela.

Alongside him, Martlé Keyter and Waheed Hoosen were elected as Deputy Presidents.

All seven National Office Bearer positions were uncontested.

The newly elected President reflects on his immediate priority areas for FEDUSA.

“The first thing is to reorganise in the space of work in South Africa. It seems like we are losing, organising and unifying workers to come into unions and ultimately join federations, because we’ve got young people who seem to have lost interest in unions. The most transverse issue that is affecting everyone in our country is the rising of the cost of living. We have seen how the fuel has gone up, and that has a ripple effect so that will be of priority that through the forums and platforms we have. We start by addressing that there should be a relief.”

item.title: Oil price spike puts more pressure on local fuel prices
item.dc:creator: Preggie Moodley
item.description: Higher transport costs could add pressure to food prices.
item.content:encoded:
Brent crude’s surge above 109 dollars a barrel threatens fresh fuel price pressure for South Africa and a political headache for US President Donald Trump ahead of next month’s congressional elections.

The international benchmark jumped more than three percent on Friday as attacks on Gulf shipping and Russian refineries heightened supply concerns.

Rising energy costs could keep affordability at the centre of the American election campaign.

Attacks around the Strait of Hormuz and renewed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries are deepening concerns about oil and diesel supplies. For South Africa, sustained increases could push up petrol and diesel prices, although the rand’s exchange rate also influences the eventual adjustment.

Higher transport costs could add pressure to food prices.

In the United States, rising pump prices could undermine Trump’s affordability message and increase pressure on Republican candidates. With congressional elections on November third, fuel costs could sharpen voter frustration over the cost of living while giving Democrats an additional boost.

item.title: March and March-affiliated parolee detained after securing bail
item.dc:creator: Sipho Kekana
item.description: Nsibande was previously convicted for kidnapping and robbery in 2009.
item.content:encoded:
A parolee affiliated with the anti-immigration group, March and March, has been detained by the Department of Correctional Services after securing bail in the Durban Magistrate’s Court.

Wandile Nsibande was arrested last week with two others on public violence and incitement charges stemming from recent anti-immigration protests in Durban.

After being granted R1000 bail, Nsibande was intercepted immediately before he could leave the court.

Nsibande was previously convicted for kidnapping and robbery in 2009.

He was released on parole in April 2022 and was to remain under state supervision until 2034.

The department’s spokesperson Singabakho Nxumalo, explaining the processes of a parolee being re-arrested, says the parole board will have to decide on Nsibande’s fate.

“Parolees and probationers are subject to specific conditions with which they are required to comply at all times. Failure to adhere to parole conditions constitutes a violation. Where a violation is brought to the attention of the Department of Correctional Services, whether through non-compliance with parole conditions or where an individual is suspected of, or criminally charged with committing an offence, the person must be detained for at least 48 hours. During this period, a parole board must convene to review the individual’s parole placement and determine the appropriate course of action,” explains Nxumalo.

Meanwhile, the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA), on Thursday, denied that warrants of arrest were issued against March and March leader Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma and her husband, Xolani Zuma.

This came after the advocacy movement issued a statement suggesting warrants for the couple’s arrest had been issued.
